one_liner: C++17 2-D rigid-body physics engine derived from Box2D 2.3.2; first-party microbenchmarks show 1.2-4.9x faster steps than Box2D 2.4.1, with losses.
what_it_does: A real-time 2-D physics engine (rigid bodies, shapes, joints, contacts, continuous collision) that began as a modern-C++ port of Box2D 2.3.2 and has since diverged. The API is not drop-in: there are no pointers or b2 prefixes; bodies, shapes, joints and contacts are values referenced by IDs (BodyID, ShapeID) through free functions such as CreateBody(world, ...) and Step(world, stepConf), and World is a type-erased polymorphic value type. Real is a CMake-chosen alias (float by default, or double, long double or a custom fixed-point type), and Boost-based strongly typed units are optional.
how_it_is_fast: From reading the source: the world implementation (AabbTreeWorld) keeps bodies, shapes, contacts and manifolds in contiguous ObjectPool arrays indexed by ID, tracks island membership in std::vector<bool> bitsets, and serves per-step allocations (islands, constraints, proxy keys) from pmr pool memory resources. Box2D 2.4.1, by contrast, walks its intrusive linked list of heap bodies at least four times per Step (island-flag reset, island seeding, fixture synchronization, TOI reset) and always runs five b2Timer profiling scopes (10 gettimeofday calls) per Step. That explains most of the static-world and contact-free wins; on contact-heavy scenes the solvers are near parity (PlayRho keeps Box2D's 8 velocity and 3 position iteration Gauss-Seidel solver).
when_to_use: 2-D games or simulations that want a Box2D-v2-style engine with a value-semantic, pointer-free C++17 API and IDs instead of b2Body*.
Worlds with many static or sleeping bodies, or many contact-free movers, where per-step bookkeeping dominates (4.9x on 10,000 static bodies, 1.6-2.3x on 1,000-10,000 non-touching falling disks).
Projects that need a configurable Real type (double, long double or a fixed-point type from the author's realnumb project) or compile-time unit checking, which Box2D v2 does not offer.
Codebases that must avoid mutable global state (PlayRho removed Box2D's globals and preprocessor settings).
when_not_to_use: Contact-heavy stacking or piles: the project's own TilesRestComboGround rows have PlayRho slower than Box2D 2.4.1 (22.9 ms vs 18.9 ms at 12, 1.42 s vs 1.33 s at 36).
New projects that can use Box2D v3: it is the actively developed successor (the catalogue entry reports one- and eight-thread runs), and no PlayRho comparison against v3 exists.
If you need a stable API: master (the 2.0 line that the benchmark ran on) is documented as unstable and not for use, and the latest tag v1.1.2 still has the older Fixture-based API.

If you want maintenance or multithreading: last commit 2024-04-30, threaded island solving is compiled out (DO_THREADED is commented out), and issue #477 about an unexplained 11-38x AddPairStressTest slowdown has been open since 2023-03-19.

integration.form: static lib (or shared lib with PLAYRHO_BUILD_SHARED), built with CMake
integration.dependencies: none for the library (C++17 standard library only); optional Boost for experimental units; the benchmark uses the googlebench git submodule; Box2D only if you edit the BENCHMARK_BOX2D define
integration.platforms: any; CI builds and tests on Linux, macOS and Windows
integration.thread_safety: not documented; one World is stepped single-threaded, and calling Step or mutators while the world is locked (for example from a contact listener during Step) throws WrongState

gotchas: Small-N rows are dominated by a fixed Box2D overhead: Box2D 2.4.1's World::Step runs five b2Timer profiling scopes on every non-zero step (10 gettimeofday calls on Linux/macOS), which PlayRho does not have. An empty world steps in 74 ns (PlayRho) vs 404 ns (Box2D), so ratios like DropDisks/1 (2.7x) or WorldStepWithStatsStatic/0 (5x) say little; only the N=1000 and N=10000 rows measure engine work.

AddPairStressTest numbers swing by an order of magnitude across commits. Issue #477 (open) reports that commit 8082f1c (the Fixture-to-pair<BodyID,ShapeID> transition, which also enabled the Box2D benchmarks) made steps 16-20 of AddPairStressTestPlayRho400 11-38x slower. The author cannot tell whether this is a regression or the fix of an earlier bug that did less TOI work. The wiki's 100x row (00991d1ec) predates that commit; the cited 2.2x row (ef285b19a) follows it. Step 0 of the same test has PlayRho 1.6x slower (2.36 ms vs 1.46 ms).

The TilesRest benchmarks time world construction plus however many steps it takes for every body to fall asleep. They mix per-step cost with each engine's settling and sleep behaviour, so they are not a per-step throughput comparison.

The Box2D build is unstated, and Box2D 2.4.1's CMakeLists sets no default build type, so a plain single-config build is unoptimized, whereas PlayRho's CMake defaults to Release with -O3. Box2D winning the contact-heavy TilesRestComboGround rows suggests it was optimized in the wiki run, but this is not documented.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick PlayRho over Box2D v3.2 only if you specifically want a Box2D-v2-style engine with a pointer-free C++17 value-semantic API, a pluggable Real type or typed units; Box2D v3 is maintained and multithreaded. Jolt Physics, Bullet, ODE and PhysX are 3-D engines and not substitutes for a 2-D game engine.
verified_claims_summary: These are the author's own Google Benchmark runs on the project wiki (commit ef285b19a, 2021-05-25, '8 X 2600 MHz' Core i7, compiler, flags and Box2D build unstated) of PlayRho vs Box2D 2.4.1 built into the same binary. PlayRho was 4.9x faster stepping 10,000 shapeless static bodies, 1.6-2.3x faster on 1,000-10,000 non-colliding falling disks, 2.2x faster on step 18 of a 400-disk pair stress test and 1.2x faster on TilesRestOneGround/36, but 1.07-1.2x slower on TilesRestComboGround.
status_note: Stale since 2024-04-30 with an unreleased, API-breaking 2.0 master line (latest tag v1.1.2); Zlib-licensed and self-contained, so vendoring a tagged release is easy, but no published benchmark covers a tagged release or Box2D v3.
